Operator: Good day, and welcome to the NovaTel Media Inc. Q3 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are currently in a listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question-and-answer session. To ask a question, you will need to request through the phone keypad during that time. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded. I would now like to turn the call over to Alex Rivera, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Alex Rivera: Thank you, Operator. Good morning, everyone, and welcome to NovaTel Media Inc.'s Q3 Earnings Conference Call. Joining me on the call today are Sarah Thompson, Chief Executive Officer; Michael Chen, Chief Financial Officer; Dr. Lena Patel, Chief Network Officer; and other members of our leadership team. Before we begin, I would like to remind you that today's discussion may contain forward-looking statements. These statements are based on management's current expectations and are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a more complete discussion of these risks.

Sarah Thompson: Thank you, Alex, and good morning, everyone. I'm pleased to report our results for Q3. We exceeded expectations in several key areas, delivering strong service revenue growth across wireless, broadband, and enterprise segments, positive ARPU trends from our pricing and bundling strategies, robust free cash flow generation, effective operating expense management, and sustained dividend payouts with solid shareholder returns. We're seeing very positive results from our investments in 5G standalone core and converged media bundles, and their impact on customer loyalty and margins is significant. We focused on network optimization and fiber expansion to drive these outcomes. Our cost discipline is proving successful. Finally, we are strategically positioning ourselves for continued growth in telecom-media convergence amid 5G maturation and streaming consolidation. With that, I'll turn it over to Michael for the financial details.

Michael Chen: Thank you, Sarah. Turning to the financials, our revenue for the quarter was $20.1 billion, up 5.2% year-over-year. Our adjusted EBITDA was $7.8 billion, resulting in a margin of 38.8%. We are maintaining strict cost discipline. Capital expenditures were $3.9 billion, primarily allocated to 5G rollout and fiber expansion.

As we wrap up a transformative year in the telecommunications and media landscape, I'd like to dive deeper into several key areas starting with our service revenue growth. Wireless service revenue came in at $8.2 billion, up 4.5% year-over-year, reflecting solid postpaid ARPU expansion and our strongest postpaid phone net adds in nearly a year at 1.2 million, bringing our total postpaid base to 112 million with 5G penetration now at 68%. This was fueled by our aggressive mid-band C-band spectrum deployment across 85% of top markets, delivering superior speeds and premium plan migrations like NexWave Unlimited Plus bundles that integrate streaming services. Broadband service revenue grew a robust 7.9% to $4.1 billion, driven by 850,000 net RGUs from our FTTH footprint now passing 28 million locations with 52% take rates in new areas, alongside speed tier upgrades to 2 Gbps symmetrical plans averaging $72.50 per account. Enterprise service revenue surged 10.2% to $2.5 billion, our fastest-growing area at 17% of the mix, with wins like private 5G networks for major manufacturers and SD-WAN refreshes for airlines, pushing ARPU to $1,450 amid demand for edge computing and AI workloads. Overall, service revenue grew 6.2% to $14.8 billion, our 11th straight quarter of gains, powered by our converged core strategy blending wireless, broadband, and enterprise with media assets to enhance ARPU, loyalty, and cross-sell.

Shifting to ARPU trends and the impact of our pricing and bundling strategies, our blended ARPU—which spans postpaid mobile, fixed broadband, and converged media services—reached $71.50 for the quarter, up 8.2% year-over-year from $66.10. Postpaid mobile ARPU hit $58.20, a 6.8% increase, from mid-cycle price hikes of 4-7% on premium 5G plans and add-ons like advanced roaming bundles contributing 15% of upside, with churn steady at 0.85%. Fixed broadband ARPU shone at $82.40, up 10.5%, thanks to 6% hikes on legacy tiers and upgrades to gigabit fiber plans now at $110-plus, alongside our FTTH passing 18 million homes. Media and streaming ARPU rose 12.3% to $19.80, offsetting linear TV pressures through skinny bundles and FAST integrations. Pricing alone drove about 65% of the expansion, or 530 basis points, with realized increases averaging 5.2% adding $3.40 to blended ARPU—strongest in the U.S. at 9.1% to $74.20. Bundling was transformative, covering 42% of customers up from 28% last year, like our Ultimate Family Bundle at $145 blended ARPU or mobile-streaming plays lifting ARPU by $4.20, reducing churn to 1.12% best-in-class and adding 1.8 million RGUs. Technical enablers like Open RAN and edge computing allowed differentiated pricing without capex spikes, positioning us for 7-9% growth next year via 5G SA personalization and new Peacock-Max exclusives.

Free cash flow generation remains a cornerstone of our strength. For the quarter, we produced $4.2 billion, up 18% year-over-year and 12% sequentially, with trailing twelve months at $16.8 billion toward our full-year midpoint of $17.5 billion. This stemmed from $7.1 billion in adjusted operating cash flow, up 14%, on 5% revenue growth including wireless at $8.2 billion, broadband at $3.8 billion with 450,000 FTTH adds, and media at $2.3 billion from 18 million streaming subs. Capex of $2.9 billion, or 20% of revenue, declined from last year as we lap peak 5G builds—45% to wireless C-band and Open RAN, 35% to broadband, rest to media CDN tweaks improving ad fill to 92%. FCF margins expanded 320 basis points to 29% with EBITDA at 42%, aided by 65% 5G utilization and regional strength: $3.4 billion from North America, $500 million Europe, $300 million APAC. Utilization was balanced: 45% or $1.9 billion to shareholders via $1.2 billion buybacks retiring 25 million shares and $650 million dividends; 30% or $1.3 billion debt reduction dropping leverage to 2.1x; 20% or $840 million growth like spectrum and edge pilots; 5% to cash reserves now $8.5 billion. Our hybrid model yields 30%+ FCF conversion, funding efficiencies with 15% ROIC on fiber.

On operating expense management, we achieved $285 million in year-over-year savings, boosting adjusted EBITDA to $1.82 billion up 12% with 320 basis point margin expansion to 38.5%, and half-year savings at $512 million toward $950 million to $1.05 billion full-year. Network ops optimized 42% or $120 million via SDN virtualization and Open RAN slashing hardware maintenance 28%, predictive AI cutting outages 35%, and 15% tower lease consolidation saving $45 million. Content discipline took 31% or $88 million through renegotiated carriage at 15-18% lower rates, 40% shift to AVOD/FAST adding $120 million ad revenue, and AI-localized libraries cutting APAC costs 25%. SG&A efficiencies claimed 27% or $77 million with GenAI chatbots resolving 65% queries to trim 2,800 FTEs, CAC down to $265, offsetting inflation. OpEx fell to 61.5% of revenue from 65.8%, with segments at wireless 42.5%, wireline 35.2%, media 28.4%. This funds $8.2 billion capex for mmWave and edge while targeting 37-40% margins.

Finally, on dividend sustainability and shareholder returns, our approach prioritizes free cash flow to back a growing dividend and buybacks amid 5G shifts and streaming wars. Full-year adjusted FCF guidance is $12.8 billion, up 15% from $11.1 billion, covering our $2.60 annualized dividend—up 5%—4.9x with a $7.5 billion cushion after payments, payout at 58% of EPS. Yield at 4.6% tops sector 3.2%, with 7.2% five-year CAGR. Leverage at 2.3x supports flexibility. U.S. wireless FCF margins hit 32% on $52.40 ARPU and 55% 5G adoption, FWA adding $800 million; Europe EBITDA at 42% via DSS; APAC doubled to $1.1 billion post-India auctions. AI network slicing cut opex 12% saving $450 million, NovaStream at 45 million subs drove $2.3 billion content up 18%. FY24 capex $10.2 billion targets 12% ROIC, with net debt down $3.2 billion YTD. We expect a 6% dividend hike to $2.76 in Q1 '24, $3-4 billion buybacks for 8-9% yield. We've returned $18.5 billion over three years while growing EPS 11% CAGR.

Dr. Lena Patel: Thank you, Michael. I'd like to provide an update on our network performance. We have made significant progress in expanding our 5G coverage to 95% in key U.S. markets and beyond via Open RAN across 40% of macro sites, achieving 450 Mbps median speeds and 65% utilization on standalone cores. Our network reliability metrics continue to improve, with unplanned outages down 35% to 0.78% mean time to repair through AI predictive maintenance, and we're seeing increased data usage across our 120 million subscriber base, up 20% year-over-year. We're also actively working on enhancing our cybersecurity infrastructure with edge computing for low-latency AR/VR and AI orchestration on network slicing. Our team's dedication to Open RAN disaggregation, dynamic spectrum sharing, and fiber-to-the-x builds has been instrumental in achieving these results, enabling 15% capex savings per site and supporting FWA growth to 1.2 million broadband subs.

Operator: Thank you. We will now begin the question-and-answer session. To ask a question, press star then one on your telephone keypad. Our first question comes from John Martinez with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

John Martinez: Good morning. Can you discuss the competitive landscape and your strategy for maintaining ARPU momentum against T-Mobile and Comcast?

Sarah Thompson: Certainly, John. In this hyper-competitive environment with players like T-Mobile pushing mid-band 5G and Comcast advancing fiber overbuilds, our strategy centers on converged bundling and premiumization. We've maintained pricing discipline with 5-7% hikes on unlimited plans without churn spikes, bundling 42% of base into high-ARPU packages like Ultimate Family at $145, integrating Disney, Paramount, and our NovaStream OTT. This has outpaced peers, with blended ARPU up 8.2% to $71.50, while Open RAN efficiencies keep costs low. We're also leveraging media moats—45 million SVOD subs—with edge CDN for 20% lower latency, hedging cord-cutting. This positions us ahead as 5G SA enables personalized pricing and enterprise edge wins grow 10.2%.

Operator: Our next question comes from Emily Chen with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

Emily Chen: Hi, thanks for taking my question. What are your expectations for subscriber growth in the next quarter, and how will that impact free cash flow generation?

Michael Chen: We anticipate 1.5-1.8 million postpaid wireless and 900,000 broadband net adds in Q4, driven by holiday promos, FWA expansion to 2 million homes, and enterprise deals like private 5G for manufacturing. This will bolster service revenue to 6-7% YoY growth, supporting FCF of $4.5-4.8 billion quarterly toward $17.5 billion full-year. With capex moderating to 18% of revenue and opex savings adding $220-250 million, we'll sustain 29%+ margins, allocating 45% of FCF to returns—dividends and $1.5 billion buybacks—while deleveraging further to 2.0x.

Operator: Our next question comes from David Lee with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

David Lee: Can you provide an update on your fiber deployment plans and the expected ROI on those investments?

Dr. Lena Patel: Absolutely, David. Our FTTH now passes 28 million locations, up 22% year-over-year, with plans to hit 35 million by year-end via $1 billion in BEAD-subsidized greenfield builds targeting high-ARPU suburbs. We've achieved 52% take rates on new passings with 2 Gbps tiers at $110 ARPU, and hybrid fiber-coax upgrades keep 85% of 45 million subs at 1 Gbps+. ROI is tracking above 15%, outperforming initial 12% targets thanks to 5.2% revenue per account growth and bundling reducing churn to 1.4%. Partnerships with Crown Castle for mid-mile dark fiber accelerate ROI, positioning us against Starlink in exurbs while Open RAN cuts deployment costs 15%.

Alex Rivera: Thank you for your questions. That concludes our Q&A session. Sarah, would you like to provide closing remarks?

Sarah Thompson: Thank you. In closing, we are pleased with our progress this quarter—strong service growth, ARPU gains from bundling, FCF powering returns and a rock-solid dividend—and remain confident in our ability to execute our converged strategy and deliver long-term value. Thank you for your time and interest in NovaTel Media Inc.

Operator: This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
